sections.description:
Satisfaction Of Charges (Land Settlement) Rules 1962
Satisfaction Of Charges (Land Settlement)
Rules 1962
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, 25th January 1962]
S. R. O. 79 (K)/62. In exercise of the powers conferred by section
34 of the Displaced Persons (Land Settlement) Act, 1958 (XLVII of 1958), the Central
Government is pleased to make the following rules :-‑
1. Short
title and commencement. (1) These rules may be called the
Satisfaction of Charges (Land Settlement) Rules, 1962.
(2) They shall come into force at
once.
2. Definitions. In these rules, unless
there is anything repugnant in the subject or context,
(a) `Act' means the Displaced
Persons (Land Settlement) Act, 1958 (XLVII of 1958) ;
(b) `Charge' means a charge
created by a Custodian on any land acquired under subsection (1) or subsection
(2) of section 4 of the Act or any decree granted by a civil or revenue court
against such land or such compensation as is determined by the court under
subsection (3) of section 43 (A) of the Pakistan (Administration of Evacuee
Property) Act, 1957 (XII of 1957) ;
(c)`Charge-holder' means a person
in whose favour a charge has been created
;
(d) `Land' means land acquired
under subsection (1) or subsection (2) of section 4 of the Act
; and
(e) all other words and
expressions used but not defined in these rules but defined in the Act or the
Schemes made thereunder or under the Pakistan
Rehabilitation Act, 1956 (XLII of 1956), or the Pakistan (Administration of
Evacuee Property) Act, 1957 (XII of 1957), shall have the meanings respectively
assigned to them in those Acts or Schemes.
3. Applications
for satisfaction of charges. (1) The Chief Settlement Commissioner may,
by notification in the official Gazette, invite applications for the satisfaction
of charges.
(2) Such applications shall be
submitted in such form, within such period and to such Settlement Authority as
may be specified by the Chief Settlement Commissioner.
(3) The Chief Settlement
Commissioner may, by notification in the official
Gezette, specify the Settlement Authorities who
may finally dispose of applications submitted under sub-rule (2).
(4) A charge-holder in whose favour more than one charge has been created shall submit
only one application in respect of all charges created at any time in his favour disclosing therein the amounts of charges, if any,
already satisfied.
4. Extent
of satisfaction of charges. (1)
Save otherwise provided in this rule, the extent of satisfaction of the total
amount of all charges created at any time in favour
of an individual charge-holder shall be as follows :
(i) for the first five thousand rupees of the aggregate value of
all charges held by a charge-holder seventy per centum;
(ii) for
the next five thousand rupees sixty per centum;
(iii) for
the next ninety thousand rupees fifty per centum;
(iv) for
the balance of the amount twenty five per centum of such balance.
Subject to a Maximum limit of
rupees three lakhs :
Provided that the total amount
payable to a charge-holder shall not exceed fifty per centum of the transfer price of the
properties against which he holds the charge.
Exceptions :
(a) A bank in liquidation or a
co-operative bank the head office of which is situated in Pakistan shall be
deemed to be an individual charge-holder in respect of a charge held by the
bank on account of advances which were made by the bank to each evacuee
provided that such advances were made against the immovable property of the
evacuee.
(b) Subject to the maximum limit
of rupees three lakhs as aforesaid, the following
classes of charges held by a displaced person or a local shall be paid in full
(i) charges on account of principal mortgage money due from an
evacuee, and
(ii) charges on account of money paid
in cash to an evacuee for the purchase of his property, where such transaction
did not materialise.
(2) No part of a charge
representing interest and no interest on any amount payable in satisfaction of
charge shall be paid.
